cities.name: Tawang
cities.overview: A high mountain town near the Bhutan and Tibet borders, home to India's largest Buddhist monastery. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit and foreigners a Protected Area Permit.

cities.name: Ziro
cities.overview: A pine-ringed plateau in Lower Subansiri district and home of the Apatani people, known for their rice-and-fish farming and the Ziro Festival of Music.

cities.name: Itanagar
cities.overview: The state capital, in the foothills, with a brick fort and a modern Buddhist temple.

cities.name: Bomdila
cities.overview: A hill town on the road to Tawang, with monasteries and apple orchards.

cities.name: Bhalukpong
cities.overview: The foothill town at the Assam border, on the Kameng River.

cities.name: Pasighat
cities.overview: The oldest town in the state, on the Siang River as it enters the plains.

cities.name: Miao
cities.overview: A small eastern town, gateway to Namdapha.

cities.name: Mechuka
cities.overview: A remote high valley in the west of the Siang country, close to the Tibetan border.

cities.name: Tezu
cities.overview: The main town of Lohit, close to Parshuram Kund.

places.name: Tawang Monastery
places.shortDescription: India's largest Buddhist monastery, set at about 3,000 m with sweeping views over the Tawang valley.
places.description: Galden Namgyal Lhatse, as the monastery is formally known, belongs to the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism and houses several hundred monks. Its three-storey assembly hall holds a gilded statue of the Buddha about 8 m tall, and a library keeps old manuscripts and thangkas. The Torgya festival in January brings masked dances to the courtyard. Visitors need an Inner Line Permit (Indians) or a Protected Area Permit (foreigners) to enter Arunachal Pradesh.
places.history: The monastery was founded in 1680–81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso in keeping with the wishes of the fifth Dalai Lama. The sixth Dalai Lama, Tsangyang Gyatso, was born near Tawang.
places.bestTimeNote: March to May and September to October. Snow can close Sela Pass in winter.

places.name: Sela Pass
places.shortDescription: A high mountain pass at about 4,170 m on the road to Tawang, with a lake that freezes over in winter.
places.description: Sela Pass carries the only road into Tawang over the Eastern Himalaya. Prayer flags flutter at the pass gate, and the Sela Lake below it lies frozen for much of the winter. The air is thin, so take it slowly and carry warm layers even in summer. The Sela Tunnel, opened in 2024, now offers an all-weather route, but the old road over the pass remains the scenic way.
places.history: The pass is linked to the 1962 India–China war and to the story of the rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, after whom the nearby Jaswantgarh war memorial is named.
places.bestTimeNote: April to June and September to October. Heavy snow can block the pass from December to February.

location.address: Sela Pass, Tawang district, Arunachal Pradesh

places.name: Ziro Valley
places.shortDescription: A green plateau of rice fields and bamboo villages, home of the Apatani people and the Ziro Festival of Music.
places.description: Ziro sits at about 1,500 m among pine-covered hills. The Apatani people farm its flat valley floor with a remarkable rice-and-fish system that needs no draught animals or machines, and their villages such as Hong and Hari are open to respectful visitors. Older Apatani women may still wear traditional facial tattoos and nose plugs, a custom now discontinued. Every September the open-air Ziro Festival of Music draws independent musicians from across India.
places.history: The Apatani cultural landscape of Ziro has been proposed for UNESCO World Heritage status in recognition of its sustainable farming traditions.
places.bestTimeNote: March to May and September to November. The music festival is usually in late September.

location.address: Ziro, Lower Subansiri district, Arunachal Pradesh 791120

places.name: Ita Fort
places.shortDescription: An old brick fort in Itanagar, the name meaning Fort of Bricks, built in the 14th or 15th century.
places.description: Irregular brick walls and three gates are the main remains, on a hill above the town. The state museum is close by.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Nuranang Falls
places.shortDescription: A 100 m waterfall near Jang on the Tawang road, known locally as Jang Falls.
places.description: A white plunge in a bare valley, reached by a short side road. A small hydroelectric plant works at its base.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A birdwatchers' paradise in West Kameng, home to the rare Bugun liocichla, found in 2006.
places.description: Forest climbing from the foothills to high ridges, with hundreds of bird species. Camps here are basic and bird-focused.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Pakke Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve in the foothills of East Kameng, known for hornbill conservation by the Nyishi people.
places.description: Lowland forest and river, in which local Nyishi villagers protect the nests of hornbills. Its Pakke Paga festival celebrates that work.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Namdapha National Park
places.shortDescription: The largest protected area in the eastern Himalaya, where tigers, leopards, snow leopards and clouded leopards all live.
places.description: A vast rainforest in the far east, entered by road and then on foot. It's home to a flying squirrel found nowhere else.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Mouling National Park
places.shortDescription: A remote national park in Upper Siang, with deep forest and rare species.
places.description: A rarely visited forest in the mountains above the Siang River, with limited facilities. Its name comes from a peak.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Mechuka Valley
places.shortDescription: A remote valley at about 6,000 ft, close to the Tibetan border, with an old monastery.
places.description: Pine and grassland along the Siyom River, with an old Tibetan-style monastery. Road access has improved, but it's still a long way out.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Parshuram Kund
places.shortDescription: A Hindu pilgrimage site on the Lohit River, with a huge bathing fair on Makar Sankranti.
places.description: Pilgrims come from across India to bathe in the fast-flowing Lohit in January, where legend says Parashurama washed away his sin.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.

places.name: Dong Village
places.shortDescription: One of India's easternmost villages, where the country sees its earliest sunrise.
places.description: A short climb from Walong, close to the China and Myanmar borders. People come for the first sunlight in India.
places.bestTimeNote: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreign nationals a Protected Area Permit, to enter Arunachal Pradesh.
